hair-salon-1: Maya shows the stylist a photograph of a bob. She wants a trim rather than a completely new style. Omar asks about a fade and an undercut for his next appointment. The stylist explains the choices and checks how much hair Maya wants removed. Maya confirms the length before the haircut begins.
hair-salon-2: Omar reads a hairstyle chart showing cornrows, dreadlocks, and extensions. Maya chooses a braid for an event. She asks the stylist to curl the loose ends instead of straightening them. A wig and hair net are in a separate display. The stylist checks Maya's photograph before starting the requested style.
hair-salon-3: The stylist puts a hair cape around Maya and prepares a blow dryer with a diffuser. A flat iron and curling iron are nearby, but they are not needed for this appointment. Omar notices hair rollers on another station. The stylist clears unused tools away and checks that Maya is comfortable.
hair-salon-4: Maya asks about highlights and lowlights before choosing a color service. The stylist shows photographs of balayage and ombre. Omar books a root touch up for another day. Maya explains the result she wants, and the stylist discusses the process. They agree on the plan before any color is applied.
hair-salon-5: Omar sits in the salon chair while the stylist checks his haircut request. A comb, scissors, and clippers are on the station. Maya asks for a bob cut at the next chair. The stylist uses a clip to separate her hair. Both customers confirm the length they want before the cuts begin.
hair-salon-6: Maya asks which product was used after her haircut. The stylist shows her a conditioner and a leave-in product. Omar compares gel with hairspray in the shop display. He sees a serum and dry shampoo on another shelf. They check the product names and ask questions before choosing anything to take home.
hair-salon-7: Omar checks in at reception for his appointment. The receptionist finds his name in the appointment book. Maya waits while the stylist cleans the salon chair and styling station. A wash basin is at the back of the room. When the chair is ready, the receptionist tells Omar where to sit.
spa-1: Maya reads the spa menu before booking. She compares a massage with a facial and asks how long each appointment takes. Omar chooses a manicure instead of a pedicure. The receptionist explains the available times. They confirm their bookings and ask what they should bring before leaving the reception desk.
spa-2: The spa menu lists Thai massage, sports massage, and hot stone therapy. Maya asks how the appointments differ before selecting one. A facial photograph shows a clay mask and cucumber slices. Omar checks the appointment length rather than guessing from the name. The receptionist answers their questions and confirms the available times.
spa-3: Maya tours the spa before her appointment. The receptionist points out the sauna, steam room, and pool. Omar finds the locker room and shower. A relaxation room has quiet seating. They read the facility information and ask which areas are included in their bookings before putting their bags in the lockers.
spa-4: The spa receptionist explains the product names on a display. Maya compares a salt scrub, sugar scrub, and coffee scrub. A towel warmer stands behind the service counter. Omar asks about an essential oil used in an appointment. They check what the booked service includes before paying at reception.
spa-5: Maya notices a candle and diffuser in the reception area. A product display holds moisturizer, toner, cleanser, and eye cream. Omar reads the label on aloe vera gel. They use the display to practice the product names from their lesson. The receptionist answers a question about the items available to buy.
spa-6: Omar receives a robe, slippers, and a towel when he checks in. Maya puts a headband and lip balm in her bag. In the treatment room, a cushion rests on the massage table. A folded eye mask is nearby. They ask where to leave their belongings before their appointments begin.
spa-7: A stone pathway leads to the spa's quiet garden. Maya brings a bamboo mat to a yoga session. Omar joins a meditation class where the instructor introduces breathing and mindfulness vocabulary. They follow the session schedule and take a break afterward. Maya describes the garden to Omar while they collect their belongings.
spa-8: Maya checks the staff list at reception. It includes a therapist, an esthetician, and a nail technician. Omar asks where the meditation room is located. The menu also lists acupuncture and shiatsu appointments. They ask the receptionist about the services and available practitioners before deciding which appointment to book.
gym-1: Omar chooses a stationary bike for his gym session. Maya uses an elliptical machine nearby. A treadmill and rowing machine are in another row. They look at the equipment labels and ask a trainer about the controls. Maya takes an exercise mat after finishing, while Omar puts his water bottle beside his bag.
gym-2: Maya puts her bag in a locker and secures it with a lock. Omar carries a shaker bottle to the training area. A dumbbell and kettlebell are beside the weight bench. They ask the trainer which equipment their session uses. Maya checks her armband before joining the class at the scheduled time.
gym-3: Omar packs a gym towel, water bottle, and sneakers before leaving home. Maya brings wrist wraps for her session with the trainer. A shelf in the gym shop displays protein powder and weight belts. They buy nothing today because they already have what they need. After training, they collect their bags from the lockers.
gym-4: Maya checks her gym bag before class. It contains athletic shoes, track pants, and a headband. Omar puts his sports watch beside a pair of gym gloves. He leaves his jacket in the locker. They arrive early enough to change and meet the trainer before the rest of the group enters.
gym-5: The trainer writes repetition and set on the board. Omar asks how the terms differ, and the trainer explains the session plan. Maya recognizes a sit-up, burpee, and jumping jack in the illustrated guide. They check the names before starting. The trainer demonstrates the planned movements and answers the group's questions.
gym-6: Omar asks at the reception desk where to find the swimming pool. Maya meets him near the juice bar after her class. A clock hangs beside the mirror wall in the training area. They check the timetable for another visit. The sauna and steam room are in a different section of the gym.
hotel-1: Maya arrives at the hotel and walks through the lobby to the front desk. The receptionist checks her booking and gives her a key card. Omar puts their bags on a luggage cart. They wait on a sofa while the room is confirmed. Then the receptionist explains how to find the elevator.
hotel-2: Omar checks the hotel room before unpacking. He hangs clothes in the closet and asks how to use the safe. Maya finds a hair dryer beside the bathroom mirror. There is a towel near the shower and a robe on a hook. They put their bags away and leave space around the bed.
hotel-3: Maya checks the hotel facilities on a map. The restaurant is near the garden, and the gym is beside the swimming pool. Omar needs the business center before his meeting in the conference room. They agree to meet at the restaurant afterward. The receptionist gives them the opening times for each facility.
hotel-4: Omar asks when the breakfast buffet opens. Maya checks the shuttle timetable and asks at the tour desk about a city visit. The receptionist explains the wifi and parking information. They compare a single room with a double room for a future booking, then ask what is included in the advertised price.
hotel-5: Maya checks the checkout time on her booking. Omar asks a bellhop to help move their luggage to the lobby. At the front desk, they check the bill and return the key cards. Maya keeps the receipt in her bag. They wait by the entrance until their transport arrives, then collect their luggage.
laundromat-1: Maya takes her clothes to the laundromat. She chooses a washing machine and reads its controls. Omar checks the coin slot and start button on another machine. After the wash and rinse, the spin cycle removes excess water. Maya checks the clothing labels before deciding which items can go into a dryer.
laundromat-2: Omar puts socks into a mesh bag before washing them. Maya measures detergent with a measuring cup. She takes a hanger for her shirt and clothespins for the drying line at home. A lint roller is in her bag. They keep clean clothes separate from the items that still need washing.
laundromat-3: Maya sorts the clothes before loading the machine. Omar checks an item that needs a pre soak. When the wash finishes, they unload the clothes. Maya folds the dry items, while Omar hangs the others. He leaves a shirt aside to iron later and checks that nothing remains in the drum.
laundromat-4: Omar reads a sign explaining which machine to use for delicate items. Maya checks labels on cotton and wool clothing. A clock shows that their wash will finish soon. At lost and found, Omar asks about a missing scarf. They put empty packaging in the trash can before collecting their clothes.
laundromat-5: Maya sets a timer so she knows when to return to the machine. Omar brings a basket for the clean clothes. When the cycle ends, they check the drum for small items. Maya puts her clothes in the basket and folds them at the table. Omar checks the timer again before starting another load.
hospital-2: Maya reads a hospital directory to find the right clinic for her appointment. It lists a neurologist, an orthopedist, and an ENT specialist on different floors. Omar asks the receptionist where the physiotherapist works. The receptionist points to the map. Both visitors check the room numbers before leaving the reception area.
hospital-3: Omar follows the signs to a patient room. He passes the laboratory and radiology department on the way. Maya is waiting near the consulting room. They check the visitor information before entering the ward. Later, they meet in the cafeteria and ask where the hospital pharmacy is located.
hospital-4: A hospital guide shows the class photographs of a stethoscope, a syringe, and a thermometer. Maya matches the words to the pictures. Omar identifies a wheelchair and a stretcher. Another photograph shows an oxygen mask and an IV drip. They use the labels to describe the equipment in complete English sentences.
hospital-5: Omar learns the names pulse oximeter, ECG machine, and nebulizer from illustrated cards. Maya compares a surgical mask with an oxygen mask from an earlier lesson. A separate diagram shows the heart, lungs, and brain. They group the cards into equipment and body parts, then check their choices with the teacher.
hospital-6: Maya labels a diagram showing the liver, kidneys, stomach, and intestines. Omar identifies the spine and muscles on another drawing. The lesson also introduces fracture, allergy, and rash as words used in health conversations. They practice describing a picture clearly rather than trying to diagnose a person from it.
hospital-7: The receptionist gives Omar directions to the blood test room. Maya has an appointment for an X-ray in another department. A poster lists ultrasound and MRI scan as other services. They check their appointment details and ask where to wait. The receptionist explains that the nurse will call their names.
hospital-8: Omar visits a relative in hospital. A chart and clipboard are beside the hospital bed. There is a pillow and blanket on the bed and a gown in the cupboard. Maya checks the visitor information. Their relative has a CT scan scheduled later, so they keep the visit short and agree to return tomorrow.
hospital-9: Maya attends workplace orientation in a hospital. The guide identifies a face shield, hand sanitizer, and a sharps container. Omar locates the call button beside a patient's bed. A wristband carries the patient's details. They ask the guide about the IV pole and oxygen tank before writing the equipment names in their notes.
pharmacy-1: Omar takes a prescription to the pharmacy. The pharmacist checks it and explains whether the medicine is a tablet, capsule, or syrup. Maya waits nearby and reads a product label. She sees cream and ointment in a different section. Omar asks the pharmacist his questions before collecting the prescribed medicine.
pharmacy-2: Maya waits at the prescription counter. Behind it, a medicine shelf holds labeled packages, and a refrigerator stores other products. Omar notices a mortar and pestle in a display about pharmacy work. The pharmacist places an ointment tube in a bag and checks the customer's details before handing it over.
pharmacy-3: Omar reads the pharmacy signs to find the right counter. A pharmacist checks a patient profile before serving a customer. Maya buys a bandage and a thermometer from the shop area. She sees a digital scale behind the counter. The refrigerated medicine stays in a separate section managed by the pharmacy staff.
pharmacy-4: Maya compares the words on pharmacy labels. A vitamin supplement is on one shelf and a herbal remedy on another. Omar asks the pharmacist about a product instead of choosing from the name alone. The lesson introduces antibiotic, painkiller, and antihistamine as different medicine terms. They write each word beside its definition.
pharmacy-5: Omar asks where to find contact lens solution. Maya looks for a throat lozenge near the cough syrup. A pharmacist is helping another customer with a prescription. The learners use the words on their shopping lists to ask clear questions. They check each product label before taking it to the counter.
pharmacy-6: A delivery driver brings boxes to the pharmacy. The stock clerk checks them while a pharmacy assistant helps customers. The manager speaks to a consultant in the office. Maya asks which worker can answer a medicine question. The assistant directs her to the pharmacist and shows her where to wait.
pharmacy-7: Maya leaves her prescription at prescription drop-off and waits near the pick-up counter. Omar takes a shopping basket for other items. A health poster is beside the entrance. When Maya's order is ready, she collects the bag and receipt. They leave through the doorway marked for wheelchair access.
pharmacy-8: The pharmacist checks the prescription and the label on a medicine bottle. Omar asks about the dosage and a future refill. Maya books a consultation for another day. Behind the counter, a mortar and pestle are on a work surface. The pharmacist finishes checking the order before handing Omar his bag.
dentist-1: Maya learns dental equipment names before her appointment. A picture shows a dental mirror, probe, and scaler on a tray. Another shows a dental drill and suction tube. Omar matches the labels to the pictures in class. They ask the teacher which names refer to tools for looking and which refer to other dental work.
dentist-2: Omar sits in the dental chair while the dentist adjusts the overhead light. A monitor and rinse bowl are nearby. Maya reads a picture guide showing an X-ray machine and dental lamp. The dental assistant prepares the tray table. Omar asks what will happen next, and the dentist explains the planned examination.
dentist-3: Maya compares a toothbrush, toothpaste, and dental floss in a vocabulary exercise. Omar identifies mouthwash and dental wax in pictures. A separate photograph shows a sterilizer and an autoclave used in a clinic. They keep the home-care products in one group and the clinic equipment in another before checking the labels.
dentist-4: The receptionist welcomes Omar to the clinic. A dental assistant takes him to the dentist. Maya asks about an appointment with the dental hygienist. The dentist explains a night guard and a temporary filling using pictures. Omar listens and asks questions before agreeing to the proposed treatment plan.
dentist-5: Maya studies a tooth diagram and identifies a molar, canine, and incisor. Omar reads about dental specialists, including an endodontist and a pediatric dentist. They compare the specialist names with their descriptions. A dental nurse helps a visitor nearby, while the radiographer prepares the room for the next appointment.
dentist-6: Omar labels a premolar, wisdom tooth, and baby tooth on separate diagrams. Maya finds the palate and uvula on a mouth drawing. Their next picture shows dentin and cementum inside a tooth. They check each label against the key, then return to the waiting room before the dentist calls them.
dentist-7: Maya completes an insurance form on a clipboard in the waiting room. The receptionist checks her dental records and appointment details. In the consultation room, the dentist explains the treatment plan and consent form. Maya asks a question about the next visit. The receptionist writes down the date before she leaves.
dentist-8: Omar has a dental checkup and asks about cleaning. The dentist explains a cavity using a drawing. Maya learns the words extraction, whitening, and sealant in her language lesson. They compare the descriptions rather than treating the words as interchangeable. Omar books another appointment and keeps the clinic's written information.
dental-clinic-1: Maya reads a clinic information sheet that lists cleaning, filling, and extraction. Another section describes a crown, bridge, and implant. She asks the dentist which term appears in her treatment plan. The dentist explains it with a diagram. Maya writes the name down so she can understand the appointment information later.
dental-clinic-2: Omar looks at pictures of a dental mirror, probe, scaler, and drill. A photograph also shows suction equipment and an X-ray machine. In the vocabulary lesson, he matches each name to its purpose. Maya reads about tooth reshaping and fluoride treatment. The teacher checks that they can distinguish treatments from tools.
dental-clinic-3: A diagram labels a molar, incisor, canine, and wisdom tooth. Maya checks the tooth names first. Omar then matches periosteal elevator and bone file to equipment photographs. The lesson also introduces a dental handpiece and an ultrasonic scaler. They place the tool cards beside their descriptions and compare the answers with the key.
dental-clinic-4: Omar studies a drawing of a tooth in the jaw. He labels the dental pulp and tooth socket. Maya identifies the gingiva and alveolar bone around it. Another diagram shows the maxilla and mandible. The class uses separate labels for the tooth, the surrounding tissues, and the upper and lower jaws.
dental-clinic-5: Maya reads a leaflet about orthodontic equipment. It shows ceramic braces and lingual braces in different pictures. Omar identifies a spacer and an expander in a vocabulary activity. They compare these with a bite plate and a mold. The lesson asks them to explain which picture matches each term before checking the key.
dental-clinic-6: Omar buys a toothbrush and asks about dental floss. Maya compares a tongue scraper with a water flosser in a product display. During class, they learn the difference between plaque, tartar, and a cavity from illustrated descriptions. They write a separate note for each term so the meanings remain clear.
dental-clinic-7: The dental assistant prepares a tray, gloves, and a bib. The dentist adjusts the light while Omar sits in the chair. Maya checks an appointment card in the waiting room. An insurance form is on the reception counter. The receptionist confirms the next visit and gives Maya the card to take home.
dental-clinic-8: During orientation, the dental team checks the location of the emergency kit. Maya learns the equipment name from a photograph in her language lesson. Omar writes a sentence about where the kit is stored. They compare their descriptions with the picture, then ask the instructor which staff members are responsible for checking its contents.
eye-doctor-1: Omar visits the eye doctor for an examination. He reads letters on an eye chart and looks through a phoropter. The doctor uses a slit lamp for another part of the examination. Maya learns these names from equipment photographs. Omar asks what the next test involves before following the doctor's instructions.
eye-doctor-2: Maya compares glasses and contact lenses at the clinic. She looks at different frames and chooses a case for her glasses. In class, Omar identifies an Amsler grid and Ishihara plates from pictures. They separate equipment used for testing vision from items people wear, then compare their answers with the key.
eye-doctor-3: Omar asks about reading glasses at the clinic. Maya looks at safety goggles for work. A display also shows swimming goggles and transition lenses. They learn nearsighted, farsighted, and astigmatism from the clinic's information sheet. Each term has a different meaning, so they write separate definitions in their vocabulary notes.
eye-doctor-4: Maya reads a vocabulary sheet about eye conditions. It includes floaters, conjunctivitis, and a stye, each with its own description. Omar checks the meaning of retinal detachment. They do not use the terms interchangeably. The teacher asks them to match each term to the information provided and explain how the descriptions differ.
eye-doctor-5: Omar reads the appointment information before visiting the clinic. The leaflet explains corrective lenses and dilation drops. Another section introduces cataract surgery, LASIK, and PRK surgery. Maya practices asking what a term means in English. At the clinic, Omar takes his questions to the eye-care professional before making decisions about treatment.
eye-doctor-6: Maya labels a diagram of the eye. She identifies the iris, pupil, cornea, and retina. Omar marks the optic nerve on another drawing. An eyelid, eyelash, and tear duct are shown in a front view. They compare the views to understand which structures are visible from outside and which are inside the eye.
eye-doctor-7: Omar waits in the waiting room while Maya looks at the display wall. A worker brings a trial frame to the examination chair. In a lesson diagram, Maya identifies the fovea, blind spot, and lacrimal gland. She keeps those labels separate from the clinic furniture names before checking her vocabulary notes.
eye-doctor-8: The clinic's work area has a lens edger, a pupilometer, and a lensometer. An assistant explains the names during a tour. Maya sees a frame display near the reception desk. Omar watches a worker organize adjustment tools beside an ultrasonic cleaner. They record the equipment names and match them to the photographs from their lesson.
human-body-head-and-face-2: Maya studies a diagram of the eye. She identifies the iris, retina, and cornea. Another diagram shows a tear duct beside the eye. Omar labels the nose, nostril, and mouth on a face drawing. They compare their answers with the key, then practice describing where each part is located.
human-body-head-and-face-3: Omar reads a diagram showing the outer ear, ear canal, and eardrum. The text explains how sound waves travel through the ear. Maya identifies the inner ear on another diagram. They match the labels carefully and ask their teacher about hearing and balance before completing the short vocabulary exercise.
human-body-head-and-face-4: Maya looks at a dental diagram and finds a baby tooth and a wisdom tooth. She labels the enamel and root on a larger drawing. Omar uses a face picture to identify a beard, hairline, and mustache. They keep the dental labels separate from the hair words to make their notes easier to read.
human-body-upper-body-1: The class labels a diagram of the upper body. Omar identifies the chest and ribcage, while Maya finds the abdomen and waist. A second drawing shows the sternum and collarbone. They use the diagram to describe each location, then check their labels against the teacher's answer key.
human-body-upper-body-2: Maya studies a drawing of the arm. She labels the elbow, forearm, and wrist. Omar finds the spine on a back diagram and marks the upper back and lower back. The teacher asks them to compare the drawings. They explain which labels refer to an arm and which refer to the back.
human-body-upper-body-3: Omar reads a muscle diagram. He identifies the pectoral muscles in the chest and an oblique muscle at the side of the abdomen. Maya labels the trapezius and rotator cuff on another drawing. The teacher explains the terms flexor and extensor. They group the labels by location before checking their answers.
human-body-upper-body-4: In a language class, Maya compares pictures showing a scar and a wrinkle. Omar sees a photograph of goosebumps on an arm. Another picture shows sunburn. They describe the visible differences using short sentences. The teacher asks them to match the words to the pictures and explain how they made each choice.
human-body-lower-body-1: Omar labels the thigh and femur on a body diagram. Maya finds the hip joint and the muscles around it. They compare the inner thigh with the outer thigh, then identify the hamstring on the back of the leg. The class checks each location before moving to a drawing of the lower leg.
human-body-lower-body-2: Maya studies a lower-leg diagram and labels the fibula. Omar finds the Achilles tendon above the heel. Another drawing shows a ligament and the meniscus near the knee. They compare the ankle, heel, and sole on a foot picture. The teacher helps them separate names of bones, joints, and soft tissues.
human-body-lower-body-3: The teacher shows a drawing of a foot. Omar labels the big toe, little toe, and toenail. Maya reads descriptions of a blister and a callus. They match each description to a separate picture. A toe joint is marked on another diagram so the class can compare skin features with structures inside the foot.
human-body-lower-body-4: Omar reads movement instructions in a language lesson. One picture shows a person kneeling, and another shows a person crouching. Maya uses kick, stride, and tiptoe to describe three other pictures. They choose the word that best describes each movement, then explain the difference between walking with long steps and walking on the toes.
human-body-hands-and-feet-1: Maya labels a hand drawing with palm, wrist, thumb, and index finger. Omar adds middle finger and knuckle. They turn to a photograph showing the back of a hand. The teacher asks which side contains the palm. Both learners compare the photograph with their drawing before checking the remaining finger labels.
human-body-hands-and-feet-2: Omar uses grip and grasp to describe someone holding a handle. Maya chooses pinch for a picture of fingers holding a tiny object. Another image shows a person squeezing a soft ball. On a hand diagram, they identify a joint, a crease, and webbing. They separate the movement words from the body-part labels.
human-body-hands-and-feet-3: The class studies a diagram of a foot. Maya identifies the heel, sole, and arch. Omar finds the ankle and toes. A side view makes the instep easier to see. They compare the two views and describe where each part is located. Then they place the labels on a drawing without looking at the key.
human-body-hands-and-feet-4: Maya reads labels on hand-care products in a shop. She compares moisturizer with hand cream and notices a bottle of cuticle oil. Omar identifies a pumice stone by its rough surface. They ask the assistant what each product is called, then write the names beside the product pictures in their vocabulary notes.
physical-appearance-1: Maya and Omar describe people in a set of photographs. One person is tall, another is short, and a third is of average height. They use slim, stocky, and muscular for different builds. The teacher asks for neutral descriptions of visible features. They compare their sentences and avoid guessing anything about the people.
physical-appearance-2: A hair-color display helps Maya learn blonde, brunette, and auburn. Omar compares photographs of fine hair and coarse hair. They also see examples of frizzy and silky hair. Maya writes one description for each photograph. The teacher checks that the color words and texture words refer to the correct features.
physical-appearance-3: Omar looks at a hairstyle chart. One photograph shows a ponytail, another a braid, and another a bun. Maya identifies a bob cut and a crew cut. The chart also includes an afro and dreadlocks. They choose a different photograph each and describe it without repeating every hairstyle in one sentence.
physical-appearance-4: Maya practices describing faces from photographs. She notices dark eyes and a round face in one picture. Omar chooses a picture with an oval face and high cheekbones. They compare a square jaw with a softer outline. Each learner writes a short description and checks that it matches the selected photograph.
skin-hair-1: At a shop, Maya compares labels for oily skin, dry skin, and combination skin. Omar finds products marked for normal skin, sensitive skin, and acne-prone skin. The assistant explains the words on the labels without choosing a product for them. They write the terms in their vocabulary notes and match them to the definitions from class.
skin-hair-2: Maya compares shampoo and conditioner bottles at the shop. She also sees a hair mask and a serum. In a separate vocabulary exercise, Omar matches bruise, scar, and stretch mark to descriptions. They keep product names on one page and skin features on another so they can revise the two groups separately.
skin-hair-3: Omar puts a comb and a brush in his bag before a trip. Maya packs a hair dryer and a hair tie. She leaves the flat iron and curling iron at home. A bobby pin is on the table beside a headband. They check the bag again before closing it.
skin-hair-4: Maya looks at four skin-care product labels. One says face mask, another eye cream, another lip balm, and another night cream. She matches the names to product photographs in her language lesson. Omar writes a short description of the lip balm container. The teacher checks their answers before the next activity.
shopping-mall-1: Maya goes to the clothing store to buy a jacket. Omar visits the bookstore while she shops. They agree to meet near the pharmacy. On the way, Maya passes a shoe store and a jewelry store. She checks the directory rather than walking through every section of the mall.
shopping-mall-2: Omar enters the mall from the parking garage. He checks the signs for the restroom and food court. Maya finds a table while he collects lunch on a tray. They note the nearest exit before leaving. The security office is near the entrance, where visitors can ask for help.
shopping-mall-3: Maya takes a jacket from a hanger and checks the size tag. She tries it on in the fitting room, then looks at the sale sign. At the checkout, she pays with a credit card and keeps the receipt. Omar carries the shopping bag while Maya puts her wallet away.
shopping-mall-4: Omar meets Maya near the photo booth. They compare activities at the mini golf area and climbing wall before choosing mini golf. A security guard gives directions to the entrance. A cashier checks their tickets, while a janitor cleans a nearby walkway. They wait until the path is clear before going inside.
meat-seafood-1: Maya plans dinner for her family. She compares chicken, turkey, and duck at the shop, then chooses chicken breast. Omar asks the butcher about beef and lamb for a different meal. They check the labels and ask for separate packages. At home, they put the food in the refrigerator before preparing anything else.
meat-seafood-2: The fish counter has salmon, tuna, and cod. Omar chooses salmon and asks how much he needs for two people. Maya looks at shrimp and mussels for another meal. At the meat counter, she buys ground beef. They keep the seafood and meat in separate packages and check that their order is correct.
meat-seafood-3: The deli sells sausage, ham, and salami. Omar asks which meat is in each product because he wants to choose carefully. He leaves the bacon and buys a beef sausage. Maya asks for a chicken fillet from a different counter. The worker checks the labels with them before wrapping their purchases.
meat-seafood-4: The butcher explains how the meat is prepared. Diced meat is cut into small cubes, sliced meat into thin pieces, and ground meat into much smaller pieces. Maya chooses diced meat for a stew. Omar asks about a rack of lamb and a piece of loin, then checks the price before deciding.
grains-dairy-1: Omar buys oats for breakfast and rice for dinner. He sees wheat, barley, and quinoa on the next shelf. He chooses quinoa for a salad he wants to try. At the bread counter, he buys a baguette. He already has toast at home, so he does not need another loaf today.
grains-dairy-2: Maya chooses pita for lunch and spaghetti for dinner. She compares penne and macaroni but keeps the spaghetti. The shop also sells ravioli and lasagna. A small roll will go with her soup tomorrow. She checks the cooking times on the pasta packages before putting everything into her basket.
grains-dairy-3: Omar makes a list before shopping. He needs milk, yogurt, and butter for the week. Maya asks him to buy cream cheese and tofu too. He picks up an egg carton and checks that no eggs are broken. The ice cream is his final item, so he goes straight home after paying.
grains-dairy-4: Maya invites a friend who prefers plant milk. She compares almond milk, oat milk, and soy milk, then chooses oat milk for their drinks. She also finds seitan in the chilled section. She reads its ingredients before buying it. At home, she keeps the food ready for her friend's visit.
beverages-1: Omar starts the morning with coffee. Maya prefers tea, and their guest asks for hot chocolate. At the café, the barista offers a latte or cappuccino too. Omar chooses an espresso this time. Maya orders herbal tea and a glass of water. They collect their drinks and find a quiet table.
beverages-2: Maya buys orange juice and apple juice for breakfast. Omar chooses sparkling water for lunch. He sees a smoothie and cold brew in the chilled display but buys neither today. Maya reads the label on a bottle of grape juice. They compare the bottle sizes before taking the drinks to the checkout.
beverages-3: The menu separates soft drinks from alcoholic drinks. Maya chooses ginger ale, and Omar orders coconut water. Another table orders beer and wine. The server checks each order before bringing it. Maya asks for water as well because she wants a second drink without choosing another sweet option.
beverages-4: At a bar, a customer reads the cocktail menu and asks what is in one drink. The bartender explains that it contains rum. Other drinks on the menu use gin, tequila, or brandy. The customer asks for a version without alcohol instead. The bartender confirms the request before preparing the drink.
kitchen-utensils-1: Maya uses a paring knife to peel a piece of fruit. A bread knife is for the loaf on the cutting board. Omar takes a frying pan for the eggs and a saucepan for water. The peeler and grater are in a drawer. They put each tool back after cleaning the kitchen.
kitchen-utensils-2: Omar makes soup in a pot and serves it with a ladle. Maya uses tongs to lift vegetables and a wooden spoon to stir a sauce. A colander drains the pasta. The baking sheet is for dinner rolls. They keep the rolling pin and whisk on the counter until their cooking is finished.
kitchen-utensils-3: Maya reads a recipe and uses a measuring cup for flour. A measuring spoon helps with a small amount of spice. Omar checks the kitchen scale and sets a timer. The blender makes a sauce, while the kettle heats water. They check their measurements before mixing the ingredients together.
kitchen-utensils-4: Omar puts rice in the rice cooker and starts it. Maya uses a juicer for fruit, then makes coffee with the coffee maker. They plan to use the slow cooker for dinner. The waffle iron stays in the cupboard today. They leave space on the counter for serving their breakfast.
cooking-methods-1: Maya reads three cooking instructions. She will boil water for pasta, simmer the sauce, and steam the vegetables. Omar plans to bake bread and roast a tray of potatoes. They compare the cooking times before starting. The sauce needs gentle heat, so Maya checks it while the other food cooks.
cooking-methods-2: Omar wants to stir-fry vegetables for lunch. He prepares the ingredients before heating the pan. Maya plans to sauté mushrooms and pan fry a piece of fish. They discuss deep fry and barbecue as methods for other meals. Today they choose quick methods because they have little time before work.
cooking-methods-3: The recipe asks Maya to chop an onion, dice a carrot, and mince garlic. Omar will peel and grate a potato. They also need to slice a lemon and zest its peel. Once everything is ready, they mix the ingredients. Maya stirs the bowl while Omar cleans the cutting board.
cooking-methods-4: Maya will beat the eggs and cream the butter with sugar. Omar uses a spoon to toss a salad gently. The dinner recipe says to marinate the vegetables before cooking and glaze them afterward. They read each instruction first and arrange the ingredients in the order they will use them.
seasonings-condiments-1: Omar tastes the soup and adds a little salt and black pepper. Maya chooses cumin and paprika for another dish. Cinnamon is for the dessert, so she keeps it separate. Fresh basil and parsley are on the counter. They label the spice jars before putting them back in the cupboard.
seasonings-condiments-2: Maya prepares a salad with dill and mint. Omar puts mustard and mayonnaise on the table for sandwiches. He also brings ketchup, but the soy sauce stays in the kitchen for dinner. A guest asks for hot sauce. Maya passes the bottle and explains that the salad already has dressing.
seasonings-condiments-3: Omar mixes olive oil with balsamic vinegar for a salad. Maya compares vegetable oil and coconut oil for cooking. She uses honey in her tea and saves the maple syrup for pancakes. They check which bottles are nearly empty and write a shopping list before putting everything away.
seasonings-condiments-4: Maya spreads peanut butter on toast. Omar chooses marmalade instead. On the shelf, they also have Nutella, molasses, and agave syrup. Maya checks the labels before making breakfast for a guest. She asks what the guest prefers rather than adding a spread without checking. They sit down once all the plates are ready.
seasons-weather-1: Maya plans a visit in spring rather than summer. She likes mild weather and wants to avoid the rainy season. Omar checks whether autumn might be better for their trip. In winter, the destination can be snowy and windy. They compare the months and choose a date before buying tickets.
seasons-weather-2: The forecast says tomorrow will be foggy in the morning and stormy later. Maya postpones her outdoor meeting. Omar sees lightning in the distance and hears thunder soon after. They check the forecast again before traveling. A clear day would suit their plans better, so they choose another date.
seasons-weather-3: Omar checks the thermometer. It is cold outside, but the room temperature is comfortable. Maya takes a coat because the evening may be freezing. In a weather lesson, they compare a barometer, a rain gauge, and an anemometer. Each instrument measures something different, so they match the names to their purposes.
seasons-weather-4: Maya opens a weather app before leaving home. Its forecast shows rain in the afternoon. Omar looks at a weather map and a radar image to see where the rain is moving. A satellite image shows the clouds. They decide to hold their meeting indoors and check the forecast again later.
weather-station-1: The morning begins with sunshine and a clear sky. A warm breeze moves through the garden. Later, clouds arrive and a little drizzle falls. By lunchtime, a downpour leaves a puddle near the gate. Maya waits indoors, then checks the road before walking to the bus stop with Omar.
weather-station-2: Omar takes an umbrella and wears rain boots because the road is wet. A rainbow appears when the rain stops. In winter, this area sometimes has snow, frost, and icicles. Maya compares photographs of a snowflake and hail during her lesson. She labels the pictures before writing a short weather report.
weather-station-3: The weather-station worker checks the thermometer, barometer, and rain gauge. Strong wind moves the weather vane. The forecast mentions a thunderstorm, so the team watches the radar. They record wind speed and rainfall rather than guessing from the sky alone. At the end of the shift, they compare the measurements.
weather-station-4: A worker checks the hygrometer to record humidity. The wind sock shows the wind's direction, while a weather balloon carries instruments above the ground. The team records temperature and cloud cover throughout the day. They compare today's data with winter and summer records to understand how the conditions change.
weather-station-5: Maya writes a short forecast. The morning will be sunny, but the afternoon may be cloudy and windy. Omar checks a radar image for rain. A satellite image shows a large band of clouds. They add the information to their report, then check whether tomorrow morning is likely to be foggy.
community-center-1: Maya visits the community center to choose a course. The art room has a painting class, and the kitchen hosts a cooking class. Omar prefers the computer lab. They ask about a dance class in the gymnasium too. Before enrolling, they check the timetable and find a course that fits their work schedules.
community-center-2: Omar joins a language class and a book club. Maya chooses table tennis instead of volleyball. The center also offers meditation and film night. They compare the activity times before paying. On Tuesday, Omar brings his book, while Maya takes her sports clothes for a game after work.
community-center-3: The community center plans a bake sale and a talent show. Volunteers put a notice on the bulletin board. A stage is ready for singers, and an exhibition fills another room. Maya offers to help at the farmers market. Omar asks the coordinator where the workshop will take place.
community-center-4: The coordinator checks the projector, microphone, and speaker before the event. A volunteer writes the schedule on a whiteboard. The instructor welcomes members at the door, while the receptionist answers questions. Omar helps move chairs, and Maya checks the clock. Everyone knows which task to finish before the audience arrives.
police-station-1: Maya visits the police station to report a lost bag. A police officer takes the details in a notebook. A detective speaks with another visitor nearby. The dispatcher uses a radio to contact the patrol team. Maya describes where she last saw her bag and checks the report before leaving.
police-station-2: During a station visit, Omar sees a patrol car, a motorcycle, and a bicycle used by officers. A guide explains a body camera and a protective vest. The ambulance belongs to a different emergency team. Omar asks how the dispatcher decides which vehicle to send, and the guide explains that situations differ.
police-station-3: Maya speaks to a worker at the front desk. She waits while an officer finds her report. On a guided tour, visitors learn about the evidence room and dispatch center. The guide explains that a holding cell is a secure room used temporarily. Visitors stay in the public area throughout the visit.
police-station-4: An officer writes details in a notebook and checks an ID card. Outside, a traffic light stands beside a crosswalk. A stop sign and speed limit sign help drivers follow road rules. A cone and barrier mark an area that is closed. Maya follows the open path back to the bus stop.
first-aid-room-1: In a vocabulary lesson, Maya opens a first aid kit with the instructor. They identify a bandage, gauze, adhesive tape, and scissors. Omar matches each item to its picture. A cold pack is in another compartment. The instructor explains that recognizing the supplies is different from knowing when and how to use them.
first-aid-room-2: Omar tours the first-aid room during workplace orientation. He sees a stretcher, a wheelchair, and a pair of crutches. The instructor points out a thermometer and a pulse oximeter. Maya locates the eye wash station. They learn the equipment names and where to find the staff responsible for medical help.
first-aid-room-3: The instructor shows pictures of an AED, a blood glucose monitor, and a blood pressure cuff. Maya matches each name to the correct device. Omar finds the first aid manual beside a box of sterile gloves. They practice describing what they can see, while the trained instructor answers questions about the equipment.
first-aid-room-4: A first-aid room has an oxygen mask, an oxygen tank, and an emergency blanket. A defibrillator is clearly marked nearby. During orientation, the instructor identifies these items and explains who is trained to use them. Maya and Omar check the room's location and the contact details for the workplace emergency team.
first-aid-room-5: Maya checks the workplace emergency phone and the alarm button with an instructor. The first-aid room has an examination table, a curtain, and a sink. A soap dispenser and paper towel holder are beside the sink. Omar finds the waste bin and medicine cabinet. They record where the room is on their workplace map.
first-aid-room-6: The instructor points to a CPR poster and an emergency contact card. A privacy screen stands near the examination area. Maya identifies a sharps container and a fire extinguisher in pictures. Omar learns the words cut, bruise, and burn. The lesson asks them to name the items rather than perform a medical procedure.
first-aid-room-7: In a language lesson, Omar learns words used to describe injuries and symptoms. The pictures show a nosebleed, a bee sting, and a blister. Another card explains fainting. Maya practices telling a trained responder what happened. They learn that words such as concussion and fracture describe conditions that need appropriate medical assessment.
first-aid-room-8: The class learns expressions heard in first-aid training, including check pulse, apply pressure, and call emergency. The instructor demonstrates the language alongside approved training materials. Maya identifies gloves and a compress in a picture. Omar practices describing a situation clearly. They ask the trained instructor for guidance about the actual procedures.
spatial-relations-1: Maya compares two meeting rooms. One is large and wide, while the other is small and narrow. The large room is close to the entrance. The smaller room is far away, beside the storage area. Maya chooses the nearby room because visitors will find it more easily. Omar helps her arrange the chairs.
spatial-relations-2: Omar moves a box from a high shelf to a low one. It was out of reach, but now it is within reach. Maya places a shallow tray beside a deep bowl. They keep the table level and flat. A tall cabinet stays at the back so it will not block the window.
spatial-relations-3: Maya arranges papers in stacked trays. The files are aligned, but loose notes are scattered across the desk. Omar draws a horizontal line and a vertical line on the board. Then he adds a diagonal arrow. They compare parallel and perpendicular lines before putting the notes into clustered groups for the meeting.
bakery-1: Maya stops at the bakery before work. She buys a baguette for lunch and whole wheat bread for home. A croissant and a cinnamon roll are on the counter, but she chooses a muffin with her coffee. The baker puts the bread in one bag and the muffin in another.
bakery-2: Omar orders a birthday cake for his sister. She likes chocolate cake, but he chooses cheesecake this time. While he waits, he sees an éclair, a scone, and a lemon tart in the display case. He buys the lemon tart for himself and asks when the birthday cake will be ready.
bakery-3: Maya wants to bake a chocolate chip cookie. She buys flour, sugar, butter, and eggs. At home, she mixes the ingredients and shapes the dough. She also has a packet of crackers and a pretzel for lunch. The cookies are for her friends, so she keeps them in a separate box.
bakery-4: The baker adds baking powder and vanilla to the mixture. He uses a whisk, then a spatula to fill the muffin tin. He puts it in the oven and cleans the mixer. When the muffins cool, he adds cream with a piping bag. The chocolate muffins go on a baking tray near the counter.
coffee-shop-1: Maya meets Omar at the coffee shop. She orders a latte, and he asks for tea. The barista also offers espresso, cappuccino, and hot chocolate. Omar wants a warm drink today, so he keeps his tea order. Maya pays for both drinks, and they sit by the window to talk before work.
coffee-shop-2: Omar needs a quick lunch. He chooses a sandwich and water instead of soda. Maya orders a bagel and cold brew. They look at a croissant, a muffin, and a brownie in the display case. Maya takes the brownie home, but Omar has enough food. They collect their orders at the counter.
coffee-shop-3: The barista weighs coffee beans on a scale and puts them in the grinder. She fills the portafilter and presses the coffee with a tamper. The espresso machine makes the coffee, and the steam wand warms the milk. She pours the drink into a cup and adds a lid for the customer.
coffee-shop-4: Maya reads the menu board above the counter. She asks the barista for syrup in her coffee and takes a napkin and a stirrer. There is a tip jar near the register. She sits on the couch beside a plant. The wifi sign is nearby, and an outlet lets her charge her phone.
ice-cream-shop-1: Omar reads the ice-cream menu. He likes vanilla and chocolate, but today he chooses strawberry. Maya asks for mango sorbet in a cup. Omar wants one scoop in a cone. They pay at the counter and sit outside. Maya tastes her sorbet first, while Omar waits for a napkin before eating.
ice-cream-shop-2: Maya orders a banana split with whipped cream and a cherry. Omar chooses frozen yogurt with nuts and caramel sauce. A topping counter also has sprinkles, cookie crumble, and gummy bears. He adds only the nuts. They carry their desserts to a table and share a few pieces of banana.
ice-cream-shop-3: The customer asks for a sugar cone, but the worker offers a waffle cone or a cup. The customer chooses the cup and takes a spoon. The worker uses a scoop tool to serve ice cream from the display case. She puts a lid on the cup because the customer is taking it home.
ice-cream-shop-4: The worker writes today's flavors on the chalkboard. Customers wait in line near the counter and pay at the cash register. After choosing a dessert, they can visit the topping bar. Maya takes her cup to the outdoor seating. She sits on a bench under an umbrella and later puts her napkin in the trash can.
pizza-shop-1: Maya and Omar order a pizza to share. Maya wants a veggie pizza with pepper and onion. Omar prefers pepperoni, but they agree on margherita with extra mozzarella. They also discuss Hawaiian and four cheese. The worker repeats their order before preparing it, so both customers know which pizza they will receive.
pizza-shop-2: The cook puts flour on the prep table and rolls the dough with a rolling pin. She spreads sauce over it and adds basil. She uses a pizza peel to place the pizza in the oven. When it is ready, she puts it on a cutting board and packs the slices in a box.
pizza-shop-3: The cook takes cheese from the refrigerator and uses a grater. A mixer prepares the dough while the brick oven heats up. At a table, Omar reads the menu and orders garlic bread with dipping sauce. The server brings a plate, a napkin, and soda. Omar also asks for a small salad.
pizza-shop-4: A delivery worker checks the ticket at the counter. The pizza is on the warming rack, ready to leave. He puts the box in a delivery bag and takes his delivery bike. Inside, Maya chooses a booth near the window. The server brings a chair for her friend and answers the phone.
restaurant-1: Maya books a table for two. The host offers a booth, but she prefers a table near the window. A menu and a napkin are at each place setting. There is a candle in the centerpiece and a salt shaker beside it. Omar moves his chair closer so they can read the menu together.
restaurant-2: The waiter brings soup in a bowl and water in a glass. Maya uses a spoon for her soup. Omar has a fork and a knife for his meal. A serving tray holds extra cups and a pitcher of water. When Maya asks for tea, the waiter brings a cup and a saucer.
restaurant-3: The host welcomes the guests while the chef prepares the main course. A cook makes the side dish, and the bartender serves drinks. Maya orders an appetizer and later chooses dessert. The busser clears the empty plates. The manager checks that the guests have everything they need before the next group arrives.
restaurant-4: Omar checks his reservation at the entrance. The server writes the order on an order pad. In the kitchen, a pan is on the stove and a pot is near the oven. After dinner, Omar asks for the bill. He pays, leaves a tip, and keeps the receipt in his wallet.
restaurant-5: The cook takes vegetables from the refrigerator and washes them in the sink. She makes soup and a salad for the lunch menu. A whisk and a mixer are on the work surface. Maya orders pasta, while Omar chooses a sandwich. They ask for bread to share and take their seats.
restaurant-6: The cook tastes the sauce before serving the meal. It needs more seasoning, so she adds a little pepper. She puts dressing on the salad and adds a garnish to the plate. Maya likes the sauce but asks for the dressing on the side next time. The server writes down her request.
supermarket-1: Maya plans a fruit salad. She puts an apple, a banana, and an orange in her basket. Then she chooses grapes and a few strawberries. She sees lettuce and a tomato nearby but leaves them for another shopping trip. At home, she washes the fruit and cuts it into a bowl for lunch.
supermarket-2: Omar needs fruit for breakfast. He compares a plum and a peach, then chooses blueberries and raspberries. He adds a lemon for his tea and an avocado for lunch. Broccoli and cauliflower are in the next section. He checks his list before paying so he does not buy more than he needs.
supermarket-3: Maya buys a cucumber and a bell pepper for a salad. She also needs spinach and a mushroom for dinner. Corn is on sale, but she chooses green beans instead. A pumpkin is too large for her basket. She checks the vegetables for freshness and carries them to the checkout.
supermarket-4: Omar wants to try a new vegetable dish. He picks a beet, a leek, and some kale. He also buys an apricot and a nectarine for a snack. A jalapeño will make the dish spicy, so he takes only one. At home, he puts the fruit away before preparing the vegetables.
supermarket-5: Maya buys basil and parsley to flavor dinner. She smells rosemary but leaves it on the shelf. Mint is for her tea, and dill is for a salad. Before paying, she remembers milk and yogurt. She adds them to the basket and puts the herbs in a separate bag to protect their leaves.
supermarket-6: Omar checks the fridge before shopping. He needs butter, eggs, and cream. At the supermarket, he also chooses cottage cheese and tofu. Frozen vegetables are on his list, but frozen pizza is not. He takes the frozen food last and goes home soon after paying so it stays cold.
supermarket-7: Maya buys bread and a bagel for breakfast. She chooses oat milk instead of almond milk this week. Parmesan is for her pasta, and feta is for a salad. She already has rice and cereal at home. She checks the flour shelf, then remembers that she still has a full bag.
supermarket-8: Omar chooses oatmeal for breakfast and noodles for dinner. He buys a baguette, but leaves the pie for another day. There is pita beside the naan. He picks pita for lunch and a small bag of couscous. At the checkout, he places the bread on top so it will not be crushed.
supermarket-9: Maya visits the meat and fish section. She chooses chicken for dinner and salmon for tomorrow. She compares beef and lamb but buys neither today. Shrimp and tuna are in a separate display. The worker packs her chicken and fish separately, and Maya checks the labels before taking them home.
supermarket-10: Omar puts ground beef in his shopping cart. He asks the worker about a steak and some ribs, then chooses only the beef. He walks down an aisle past a shelf of canned food. At the checkout, the cashier scans each barcode. Omar puts the heavier items at the bottom of his bags.
supermarket-11: Maya reads the price tag and sees a sale sign. At the checkout, she gives the cashier a coupon and her loyalty card. The scanner reads each item on the conveyor belt. Maya checks the receipt before leaving. Next time, she may use self-checkout if she has only a few items.
supermarket-12: Omar buys detergent, a sponge, and dish soap. He also needs a paper towel roll and a trash bag. A mop is on sale, but his old one still works. He adds rubber gloves to his basket. At home, he puts the cleaning products in their usual cupboard, away from food.
supermarket-13: Maya takes a dustpan and a bucket from the household section. Then she chooses water and tea for the week. She leaves the soda and energy drink on the shelf. Sparkling water is for a guest who is coming tonight. Before paying, she checks that every bottle has a secure cap.
supermarket-14: Omar chooses orange juice and apple juice for a picnic. He adds crackers and popcorn for sharing. He considers chips and cookies but has enough snacks already. Maya brings mineral water from another aisle. They divide the drinks between two bags so neither person has to carry all the weight.
supermarket-15: Maya wants snacks for a train journey. She buys nuts, dried fruit, and a granola bar. She leaves the lollipop and marshmallow on the shelf. At home, she puts the nuts and dried fruit into a small container. Peanut butter and jam are for sandwiches she will make before leaving.
supermarket-16: Omar looks for ingredients for dinner. He takes canned beans, tomato sauce, and olive oil. He adds coconut milk for another meal. Ketchup and mustard are already in his cupboard. He checks the size of each can before paying because a large can would be more than he needs tonight.
supermarket-17: Maya buys salt, pepper, and vinegar for the kitchen. She chooses soy sauce for a stir-fry and cinnamon for baking. A jar of marmalade is for breakfast. She checks whether she needs sugar, then remembers the full bag at home. She returns the extra bag to the shelf before paying.
supermarket-18: Omar reads a recipe and lists cumin, paprika, and turmeric. At the shop, he also finds ginger powder and chili flakes. He chooses a small packet of each spice. Baking soda and baking powder are on a different shelf. He needs neither for this meal, so he leaves that section.
supermarket-19: Maya buys toothpaste, a toothbrush, and dental floss. She adds deodorant and sunscreen to her basket. She checks the conditioner bottle to make sure it is the one she wants. A comb is on the next shelf. She already has one at home, so she pays only for the items on her list.
supermarket-20: Omar needs lip balm and hand sanitizer. He compares a small tube with a larger bottle and chooses the smaller size for his bag. He also buys a jar of jam and a box of tea. The cashier offers a bag, but Omar already has a reusable container for carrying his shopping.
supermarket-21: Maya chooses a bunch of bananas and a loaf of bread. She asks for a dozen eggs. She uses the scale to weigh the fruit, then compares two prices. At the checkout, she unloads her basket, watches the cashier scan the items, and pays. She puts the eggs on top of the other shopping.
supermarket-22: Omar asks a stock clerk where to find bread. The baker shows him a fresh loaf, and the butcher weighs a pound of meat for him. Omar waits in line to check out. The bagger helps him pack the food. Outside, he loads the bags into his car and keeps the receipt.
supermarket-23: Maya's list includes a bunch of grapes, a head of lettuce, and a loaf of bread. She also needs a dozen eggs and a pack of crackers. She compares an organic product with another brand. A gluten-free loaf is for her guest. She checks the packaging carefully before choosing the right one.
supermarket-24: Maya asks, 'How much is this?' The cashier points to the price and explains that it is on sale. Maya checks the nutrition facts and the best before date. At the checkout, the cashier asks, 'Cash or card?' Maya pays by card and asks, 'Can I get a bag?'
supermarket-25: Omar tells the cashier, 'I have a coupon.' He also asks, 'Can I taste this?' about a sample of hummus. Later, he notices a damaged package and says, 'I need a refund.' The cashier checks the receipt. Omar then asks where to find ginger and takes his cart to the right aisle.
